newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ shares market closes flat but volume picks up.
newsitem.headline: NZ shares market closes flat but volume picks up.

text.p: * NZ sharemarket closes flat again but volume picks up
* Fletcher stocks perform well, Telecom weak
* Brokers pick market to stay flat with downside vulnerable --------------------------(April 11)----------------------------
Price movements at close
LAST CHG
Brierly Investments 128 +1 * NZSE-40 cap index -0.87 at 2,232.98
Carter Holt Harvey 307 -1 * NZSC cap index -17.28 at 4,951.57
Fletcher Challenge 289 +3 * NZSE-10 cap index -2.23 at 1,096.56
Lion Nathan 341 +1 * Volume NZ$57.4 million. Futures -6 at 1,110
Telecom 648 -6 * Other movers - +5 +5
The New Zealand share market continued on Friday to wallow at Thursday's closing level while brokers got some encouragement from higher volumes.
They expect the market to remain flat to weaker next week, where the main direction is likely to come on Tuesday from March quarter CPI data.
They blamed high bond yields, indications that first quarter results are disappointing, jittery overseas markets and comments from U.S. investment houses that the kiwi dollar is overvalued.
"It doesn't augur that well for our market," said County NatWest broker Sean Vaughan. "I would say the risk in this market is that it could fall."
The top 40 index closed 0.87 down at 2,232.98 on volume of $57.4 million.
Telecom continued to struggle following the cessation of the first stage of its share buyback programme. It was down six cents at $6.48. It will publish its annual result on May 14.
There was good turnover in Lion Nathan but its price appears capped below $3.42. It closed a cent ahead at $3.41.
Most of the Fletcher stocks performed well with Paper up three at $2.89 and Energy up five to $3.99.
Progressive Enterprises closed five cents up at $1.58 after announcing it would rationalise its supermarket chains to two from three.
The Warehouse lost 10 cents of Thursday's 52 cent gain to end at $3.62.
